idiom_name: pthread worker thread + mutex/condition-variable request queue
implementation_notes: C's thread libraries supply only primitives: pthread_create starts the scheduler thread, the activation queue is a hand-written struct guarded by a pthread_mutex_t and signalled through a pthread_cond_t, each method request is a struct holding a function pointer plus arguments and a result slot, and the future is that slot plus a completion flag the caller waits on. Methods enqueue and return; the servant functions are called only by the worker thread, so they take no lock. C11 <threads.h> (thrd_create/mtx_t/cnd_t) is the ISO alternative where POSIX is unavailable, but the six roles remain hand-written either way, which is why this is manual and not library support.
pitfalls: A condition-variable wait must be wrapped in a predicate loop; a single if-check loses wakeups (or spins) and requests are dropped or duplicated.
The request struct and its future must stay alive until the worker publishes the result - enqueueing a stack-allocated request and returning is a use-after-free.
Without an explicit stop flag plus pthread_join the process hangs at exit, and one thread per active object is a fixed resource cost that must be bounded in configuration.
